- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.5–1.5% bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.27 spikes followed by -0.16 corrections, model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
